title: Runbook seeder from trace-snapshot webhooks with PagerDuty urgency mapping
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: On high-severity incidents we spend 6-12 minutes assembling context: the right trace slices, top offending spans, recent deploys, and an actionable runbook stub. This delays mitigation and increases MTTI.

Goal: Build a Runbook Seeder service that captures sampled trace snapshots (KV/short-span context) at alert time, synthesizes a runbook template pre-filled with triage hints (likely causal services, relevant dashboards, recent config changes), and pushes it to PagerDuty incidents and Slack incident channels with urgency/impact mapping. The seeder should also create a seeded postmortem skeleton in our Confluence template and attach links to telemetry artifacts.

Non-goals: full autocompletion of final postmortem prose, replacing human judgement for severity labeling, or shipping global autoincident-resolution playbooks in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: When a PD incident is opened for alerts tagged observability:trace, the Runbook Seeder receives a webhook and stores a trace snapshot in S3 with an index key
PD incident receives a note with a runbook template link and set of triage hints (top 3 suspected services, suspect span id, relevant dashboard links)
Slack incident channel receives a message with action buttons: Attach Runbook, Create Postmortem Draft, Mark Investigation Owner
Runbook templates must include a field for urgency mapping derived from PD priority and recent error rate delta
Seeded Confluence postmortem draft created with links to trace snapshot, dashboard graphs, and the alert definition
End-to-end latency for webhook -> PD/Slack message < 8s for sampled events in normal load
Feature guarded behind a feature flag and limited to internal org first
Security review completed and no secrets are leaked in attachments
design_notes: Trace sampling: reuse runtime trace-tags 'ops.sampled=true' and capture KVcache snippet and span tree up to 250KB compressed
Webhook receiver: new lightweight 'seeder' Lambda-style service in infra account; signs outgoing messages with service key; logs audit record
Runbook template: JSON-backed template using our Confluence REST API mapping; template fields: Summary, Impact, Suspected Services, Evidence Links, Quick Mitigations, Next Steps, Owner
Urgency mapping: map PD priority (P1/P2) + 5-min error-rate delta (>3x) to urgency A/B; used for suggested mitigation and whether to auto-create postmortem draft
Attachment storage: encrypted S3 prefix with KMS key per environment; signed short-lived URLs posted to PD/Slack; no full trace dump in Slack messages
Rate limits: seeder will sample at 1 in 5 for low-frequency alerts; dynamic backoff if write rate to S3 exceeds 200/s
Observability: instrument seeder with internal metrics: webhook_count, webhook_latency, s3_write_errors, drafts_created, pd_note_delivery_latency
implementation_steps: 1) API: create /webhook endpoint in seeder service; validate PD/Slack event signatures
2) Trace grabber: hook into trace collector to request a snapshot (kv snippets + span_ids) given trace_id; compress & encrypt and push to S3
3) Template generator: render Confluence-compatible HTML and short JSON manifest for runbook fields
4) PD integration: call PagerDuty Notes API to append seeded runbook link + urgency label; include action metadata for PD responders
5) Slack integration: post to #incidents-<incident-id> with interactive buttons wired to internal ops-bot endpoints
6) Postmortem draft: call Confluence API to create a draft page using our postmortem skeleton and inject telemetry links
7) Feature flag: gate on ff.observability.runbook_seeder; CLI toggle and Console toggle for internal orgs
8) Tests: unit tests for signature validation, integration test for S3 storage + signed URLs, e2e test that simulates an alert -> PD -> Slack flow
9) Rollout: internal org -> canary subset (50 orgs) -> all internal orgs -> public beta behind usage cap
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal demo — 2026-02-10; invite SRE and oncall leads to validate UX
Phase 1: Enable for internal orgs only; monitor metrics and error budgets for 2 weeks
Phase 2: Canary to 50 customer orgs under NDA with telemetry opt-in
Phase 3: Post-trial adjustments; documentation and runbook catalog update; GA behind pricing/contract terms
metrics: Time to initial context (alert -> runbook visible in PD) target < 12s
Fraction of incidents with a seeded postmortem draft (internal orgs) > 60% after 2 weeks
Reduction in median time-to-first-action for P1 incidents by target 20% (compare historical)
S3 storage growth monitored; retention policy default 90 days
risks_mitigation: Risk: leaking sensitive payloads into Slack/PD. Mitigation: store artifacts encrypted, post only signed short URLs, redact user PII, security review required
Risk: additional latency on alerting pipeline. Mitigation: asynchronous S3 write with optimistic PD note posted; include minimal context inline if S3 write fails
Risk: noisy auto-drafts cause PM overhead. Mitigation: only create postmortem drafts for incidents above urgency threshold or explicit checkbox
Risk: cost of storing large traces. Mitigation: clip snapshots to 250KB compressed and apply TTL; sample rate defaults to 1/5
Risk: PD rate limits. Mitigation: implement batching of PD note updates and exponential backoff with jitter
qa_tests: Simulate PD incident webhook with a sampled trace_id; assert S3 artifact exists and PD note contains signed URL
Simulate PD webhook when S3 write fails to ensure Slack receives fallback summary
Verify KMS encryption/decryption of artifacts in staging
Pen test: ensure no direct trace content is visible in Slack/PD message bodies
Load test: 1k webhooks/minute burst and observe seeder latency and S3 throttling behavior
